edges.description: A 40S assembly defect is one of the two routes to the shared ribosome-insufficiency state on which the erythroid phenotype depends.
A 60S assembly defect is the other route to the shared ribosome-insufficiency state.
Failure to deliver uL5 and uL18 to the nucleus starves 60S assembly of two of its proteins, producing a phenotype the source describes as reminiscent of large-subunit ribosomal protein gene variants.
Ribosomal stress activates p53, leading to cell cycle arrest and apoptosis of erythroid progenitors.
Ribosomal protein haploinsufficiency disrupts developmental growth programs, contributing to short stature.
Ribosomal protein haploinsufficiency disrupts embryogenesis, contributing to congenital malformations.
Ribosomal protein haploinsufficiency disrupts limb development, contributing to triphalangeal thumb.
Chronic ribosomal-stress marrow dysfunction increases acute myeloid leukemia risk.
Chronic ribosomal-stress marrow dysfunction increases myelodysplasia risk.
DBA cancer predisposition includes osteosarcoma downstream of the ribosomopathy state.
Erythroid progenitor apoptosis produces the macrocytic anemia of DBA.
Selective erythroid apoptosis produces pure red cell aplasia.

Reduced full-length GATA1 impairs erythroid differentiation and produces the same red-cell aplasia as the ribosomal route, without passing through the ribosomal-stress p53 node. Only the erythroid failure is wired here; no cited source in this entry attributes the macrocytosis to GATA1.

nodes.description: A distinct non-ribosomal mechanism causing DBA. GATA1 is an X-linked erythroid transcription factor essential for erythroid differentiation. Mutations in GATA1 (including splice site variants) reduce functional GATA1 protein levels, impairing erythroid gene expression. Unlike ribosomal protein mutations, GATA1 mutations directly affect erythroid transcription rather than global translation, but converge on the same erythroid differentiation failure.

nodes.description: Haploinsufficiency of a large-subunit (60S) ribosomal protein gene impairs 28S and 5.8S rRNA maturation and 60S subunit production. The six genes on this node are the DBA genes HGNC assigns to the "L ribosomal proteins" gene group. Two of them, RPL26 and RPL15, additionally disturb a small-subunit pre-rRNA cleavage step, so the subunit split describes which protein is missing rather than a clean partition of the processing defect.

nodes.description: The convergence point of this entry: whichever ribosomal protein is missing, and whether the lesion is in the gene or in the import step that delivers the protein, the shared consequence is reduced ribosome assembly and protein synthesis capacity. Erythroid progenitors are exquisitely sensitive to that state because of their high proliferative and translational demands. Causal genes are wired to the subunit-specific upstream nodes rather than listed here, so this node carries no `genes:` list of its own.

nodes.description: The one DBA mechanism in this entry that is upstream of the ribosomal proteins themselves. HEATR3 is an import adaptor for the large-subunit proteins uL5 (RPL11) and uL18 (RPL5); biallelic HEATR3 variants destabilize it, and patient-derived fibroblasts show reduced nuclear accumulation of uL18. The consequence is a shortage of large-subunit proteins in the nucleolus rather than a shortage of their transcripts.
